transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 09:00 PT
Duration: ~44 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE); Marco Diaz (Redwood SE); Priya Shah (Redwood CSM); Tom Hargreaves (CTO, Aurelia); Maya Lin (Infra); Ravi Patel (ML); Sara O'Neill (Security); Jordan Kim (PM)

Summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on Dedicated sizing and autoscaling. Reviewed recent test runs, discussed burst scenarios and failover, asked for more telemetry and a dedicated stress test.

---Transcript---
[00:00:00] Lena: okay good morning everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 40 minutes, agenda is sizing, autoscale policies, and any security follow-ups, um Priya do you want to intro?
[00:00:12] Priya: yeah quick, this is our weekly sync, thanks all, same goals as last week, wanted to see results from the ramp and talk burst planning.
[00:00:24] Tom: hi, thanks, we've seen a couple of production-ish spikes on Tuesday where the 95th jumps, so we want to understand the dedicated option better.
[00:00:33] Marco: cool, thanks Tom, quick recap — last run we did steady-state 120 rps, then two 90s spikes to ~260 rps for five minutes, we saw tail latency go up to around 1.2s at 95th, and CPU on the host jumped, so we want to tune batch size and autoscale thresholds, right.
[00:00:49] Ravi: yeah and just to add, some of those spikes correlate with larger context windows, so tokens per request varied, it wasn't pure rps.
[00:00:58] Maya: and on infra side we have limits on peak GPU allocation for the pilot tenant, so bursting beyond reserved capacity needs approval.
[00:01:07] Lena: so two threads: one is sizing the steady reserved capacity so p99/95 targets are met for normal traffic; second is burst model, how do we allow short-lived spikes without huge cost — Marco you had a proposal?
[00:01:22] Marco: yes, proposal is dedicated pool sized for baseline 150 rps with headroom; set autoscale min nodes = 2, max = 8; scale up policy based on queued requests + 95th latency > 800ms for two consecutive sampling windows (30s windows), and burst capacity that allows short bursts up to 300 rps for 5-10 minutes by temporarily permitting burst nodes charged at on-demand rate. Also recommend prefix/KV cache to reduce duplicated tokens.
[00:01:56] Tom: hmm, 8 nodes is a lot — can you map nodes to expected rps or tokens/s?
[00:02:04] Marco: roughly each node with our quantized Llama-variant handles about 60-80 rps for short responses (<=256 tokens) with caching; so 4 nodes hit ~240-320 rps; for longer contexts throughput drops. This is approximate of course.
[00:02:21] Sara: on security we need to know what data leaves the VPC during burst — if burst uses shared pools is there any exfil?
[00:02:29] Lena: good question — for Dedicated, workloads stay in customer-dedicated VPCs; burst nodes can be in same VPC if using Dedicated Burst, otherwise fallback to Redwood-hosted spare capacity which we can restrict for customers under NDA. We'll include the network diagram.
[00:02:45] Maya: ah okay, so the burst mode can be configured to use only reserved hardware or allow external capacity — that helps. We probably need the variant that keeps everything internal.
[00:02:55] Priya: note, customer is leaning towards internal-only for compliance.
[00:03:01] Marco: noted. For autoscale thresholds, one nuance — batching behavior can mask latency signals. If batch sizes grow during spikes you might see average token latency favorable but request-level latency spikes; we recommend monitoring both per-request p95 and token throughput.
[00:03:18] Ravi: yeah we saw higher batch sizes last run which helped throughput but made some single-request tails worse. Can we cap batch size?
[00:03:25] Marco: yes you can set max batch size and max wait time; tradeoff is throughput vs tail latency. For low tail we drop max batch size to 8 and max wait 10ms; for higher efficiency you bump those up.
[00:03:36] Tom: what's the billing implication of burst nodes? how to estimate cost if we allow 10 minutes at 300 rps twice a day?
[00:03:44] Lena: we bill reserved at committed rate; burst on-demand is higher per GPU-hour. Marco will produce a cost spreadsheet mapping node counts and expected token throughput to hourly rates so you can model those burst windows.
[00:03:58] Marco: i'll attach a spreadsheet, yes. Also we can do scheduled scaling for known marketing pushes so you don't hit autoscale cold starts.
[00:04:07] Jordan: we have several planned promos that cause 5-7 minute spikes; scheduled scale would be ideal.
[00:04:13] Priya: ok next, logs/telemetry — we requested 1-minute metrics and detailed per-request traces for the pilot. Any blockers?
[00:04:22] Maya: we've been able to forward our app logs, but the Redwood agent we ran had a few missing fields — timestamps off by a second or two— not a blocker but noisy.
[00:04:32] Marco: yeah some of our SDK telemetry names are slightly different in customer's instrumentations — we'll normalize in the onboarding script.
[00:04:39] Ravi: can we get raw KV cache hit logs? that affects sizing a lot.
[00:04:43] Marco: we'll include cache hitrate telemetry in the next run.
[00:04:47] Tom: also want to make sure failover to hosted fallback doesn't leak PII; we need memos on what logs are retained.
[00:04:55] Sara: exact — SOC2 and audit log retention are key for us.
[00:04:59] Lena: we will share SOC2 summary and log retention policies; for Dedicated we can configure retention and redaction.
[00:05:06] Ravi: a question on per-route quotas — we have internal vs external routes, can we reserve capacity per-route?
[00:05:12] Marco: yes routing policies can pin routes to specific pools; you can reserve N nodes for route X which helps protect SLAs.
[00:05:20] Maya: what's the expected scale-up time from policy? we've seen about 60-90s in some systems, is that similar?
[00:05:26] Marco: with our pool warmers and pre-loaded weights we can do ~20-45s for warm nodes if using warm pool; cold starts (pulling images/weights) can be several minutes unless pre-warmed. So recommended to keep a warm buffer for critical routes.
[00:05:42] Tom: okay suggested config: baseline 3 nodes, warm buffer 1 node, max 7, burst allowed up to 300 rps for 10 min. Thoughts?
[00:05:52] Marco: seems reasonable as a starting point. We should validate with a 300 rps stress that includes variable token sizes.
[00:05:59] Priya: Marco, can you schedule that stress run?
[00:06:02] Marco: yes i'll run with two profiles: short responses (<=128 tokens) and mixed-context (up to 1024).
[00:06:08] Ravi: please include KV cache disabled run so we can see worst-case.
[00:06:12] Marco: will do.
[00:06:14] Sara: security question — KMS integration, we use HashiCorp Vault; can Redwood integrate?
[00:06:20] Lena: we support KMS integrations and bring-your-own-key via HSM in Private mode; for Dedicated we have KMS connectors (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and Vault via connectors — we'll include the integration notes.
[00:06:31] Sara: and SSO mapping — need to ensure only a small admin group can rollout models.
[00:06:35] Priya: we discussed RBAC last week, yes we support fine-grained roles; we'll send the role matrix.
[00:06:42] Jordan: also can we set automatic fallback policies — e.g., if dedicated pool can't handle spike go to smaller model rather than full hosted fallback?
[00:06:50] Marco: yes we can route to a smaller quantized variant as a fallback (cheaper/less latency guarantees). That's part of the graceful degradation policies.
[00:06:58] Tom: that's interesting, prefer model variant fallback to shared-hosted for compliance.
[00:07:03] Lena: noted. We'll document model-variant fallback options and costs.
[00:07:08] Maya: what telemetry will we get during the stress run? request latencies, per-node CPU/GPU, batch sizes, kv cache stats?
[00:07:14] Marco: yes full telemetry; we'll give prometheus metrics + per-request traces and a csv export of sample requests.
[00:07:21] Ravi: good. Question on autoscale sampling windows — you mentioned 30s windows; can we make them 15s for more aggressive scale up?
[00:07:29] Marco: yes you can, but quicker windows can increase churn and cause over-scaling for transient blips; recommend 30s with a two-window confirmation for scale-up and single window for scale-down.
[00:07:41] Tom: how do we measure cost if we keep warm nodes? a 1-node warm buffer 24/7 is expensive.
[00:07:47] Lena: we can run cost model; sometimes scheduled warm buffers during business hours is a compromise. We'll show dollar impact in spreadsheet.
[00:07:56] Priya: any blockers on Redwood side to run the 300 rps?
[00:07:59] Marco: no blockers, need the traffic profile from customer and confirmation of KV cache toggles.
[00:08:05] Maya: i'll provide spike logs and current batch settings by Friday.
[00:08:09] Ravi: i'll check in on token distribution and share a sample payload set.
[00:08:13] Tom: timeline — we want a pilot sizing and costs by next week, is that doable?
[00:08:18] Lena: yes if we get telemetry by Thursday we'll have a draft by Friday-Monday.
[00:08:24] Jordan: quick note, procurement wants rough MRR estimates for Dedicated for budgeting.
[00:08:29] Lena: we'll include a mid and high estimate.
[00:08:32] Sara: could you also confirm audit log retention lengths and encryption in transit details?
[00:08:36] Marco: ack, will include.
[00:08:38] Priya: any final questions?
[00:08:41] Maya: just to confirm, burst nodes will not attempt to connect to external shared buckets for model weights, right? we prefer local-only.
[00:08:48] Marco: yes we can ensure local-only model artifacts for Dedicated; only if you allow hosted burst would we pull from Redwood-managed buckets.
[00:08:57] Tom: ok great, that should address compliance concerns.
[00:09:00] Lena: recap — Marco to run stress tests (300 rps profiles) and attach spreadsheet; Lena to send Dedicated sizing/pricing; Maya/Ravi to provide telemetry and sample payloads; Sara to confirm KMS/SAML requirements. Next sync we'll review stress run results.
[00:09:17] Priya: thanks all, i'll follow up with calendar invites for the performance window.
[00:09:22] Meeting ends (approx 09:44)

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-heard proper nouns, and timestamps approximate. Some speech is condensed.
